Stamper restore drift

Why a hand-maintained restore list keeps losing a file · 2026-07-26

The two lists that must agree

Stamp target (from the stamper)Restored?

src/hooks/src/lib/cc-version-matrix.tsyes

Twice is a pattern. README.md was missing until it bit someone. The SKILL.md sweep was added later for the same reason. marketplace.json is the third instance of one root cause: the restore set is maintained in a second place and drifts from the list it is supposed to mirror.

Why this file matters more than the others

.claude-plugin/marketplace.json holds the engine field, the machine-readable gate Claude Code reads to decide whether ork can be installed at all. Left at a fixture value it names a version that does not exist:

  "engine": ">=2.1.220"   ← real floor
  "engine": ">=2.1.999"   ← fixture; plugin becomes uninstallable

Fix: derive, then prove

STAMP_TARGETS=()
while IFS= read -r target; do
  [ -n "$target" ] && STAMP_TARGETS+=("$target")
done < <(grep -oE "^stamp\('[^']+'" "$STAMPER_SRC" | sed "s/^stamp('//; s/'$//")
  • Derived, not enumerated — read from the stamper's own stamp('<path>') call sites, so a new target is covered the moment it is added.
  • Loud post-condition — after restoring, any target still holding a fixture version fails the run. The previous failure mode was silent.
  • Byte-exact cp -p — 7 SKILL.md files have no trailing newline, which echo "$VAR" > file silently adds.
  • No mapfile — the shebang is /bin/bash, which on macOS is bash 3.2 where mapfile does not exist. A mapfile version passes Linux CI and breaks every local run.

Honest scope: not a proven root-cause fix

marketplace.json found dirty at >=2.1.999observed
It is stamp target #5 and was absent from the restore listverified
The stamper test alone causes the leakrefuted

Refuted how. Three consecutive runs left the file clean, and an injected mid-test abort restored correctly under both the old and the new code. The actual trigger is unidentified; a concurrent session or an interrupted run are untested candidates. The missing target is real and worth closing on its own merits, and the post-condition exists so a recurrence is loud rather than silent, but this PR does not claim to have found what bit the tree.
